# Operating this repository:
# - Work happens on verb-prefixed branches, one verb per state (these are branch names, not directories):

graph:record {
	bedrock:vertex\/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace a bedrock:ontology\/Decision ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/record\/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "ADR 0001: AtomicKeyspace, O(1) terminal reads, absent/incomplete taxonomy" ;
		bedrock:references bedrock:vertex\/invariant-08-dependency-boundary , bedrock:vertex\/invariant-13-state , bedrock:vertex\/invariant-kernel-extension ;
		bedrock:source bedrock:path\/docs\/decisions\/0001-atomic-keyspace.md ;
		bedrock:statement "The kernel's keyed-I/O law, extended by human-ruled batches 1-9. Chosen: AtomicKeyspace with NO unconditional write anywhere on the module surface (create is put-if-absent, compare_exchange always carries If-Match, delete_if_match is the conditional delete-side dual); values live in envelope v2 {incarnation, version, payload} so CAS discriminates values AND eras structurally — tombstones witness deliberate destruction, incarnation counters fence cross-deletion ABA, certified trim certificates are the immutable retention floor, and lineage heads carry their own era stamp with conditional deletion tails (L9/L10/L14). O(1) terminal reads are two GETs with chain linkage below the terminal deliberately unverified; Absent, Destroyed, and StateHistoryIncomplete are distinct truths, never conflated. The application boundary is structural, not lexical: application crates cannot reach the adapter at all (KernelHandle + dependency floor) because a source token scan cannot prove capability absence. Rejected: any unconditional overwrite (reopens ABA), yeetz-sdk-core placement (dissolves the one-place assured contract boundary), lexical-only enforcement (three bypass classes compile clean), caller-discipline-only ABA safety. Measured fact (real-S3 probe, run 32423582844): Exoscale SOS etags are content hashes — the ABA case is REAL at the raw backend; the versioned/incarnated envelope is what closes it. Flips if: a backend changes etag semantics (the real-s3 probe rig re-measures and fails loudly), or a human rules the era model must move — a new ruling is a superseding vertex, never an edit here.\n" ;
		bedrock:timestamp "2026-08-21T10:51:16" .
	bedrock:vertex\/decision-0002-streams a bedrock:ontology\/Decision ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/record\/decision-0002-streams.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "ADR 0002: streams — append-only event logs on AtomicKeyspace" ;
		bedrock:references bedrock:vertex\/invariant-13-state , bedrock:vertex\/invariant-kernel-extension ;
		bedrock:requires bedrock:vertex\/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace ;
		bedrock:source bedrock:path\/docs\/decisions\/0002-streams.md ;
		bedrock:statement "The streams crate: per-stream append-only event logs as immutable, individually addressable objects at streams/v1/<id>/log/<seq:020> under the kernel keyspace root. Chosen: the event object's conditional create IS the seq allocation — no counter, no head CAS; byte-identical retries are idempotent only inside the bounded pre-scan window (beyond it, same-stable-id re-appends land as new events: at-least-once, consumers dedupe by event id; in-window payload/schema change is a typed IdempotencyConflict, never a silent second landing); complete=true requires BOTH a verified tail hint (a computed-key GET witness a frozen LIST cannot hide) AND an empty ordered probe — a LIST alone never certifies (G130); reads are typed and loud (Corrupt names missing seqs, decode failure is an error never a skip, OffsetExpired is the typed trim boundary), and a backend failing the strong-LIST contract yields BackendUnqualified rather than false completeness. Certified trim (batch 5): immutable trims/ certificates are the floor, GC deletes only below it, trim-to-end is logically empty with appends landing AT the floor (finding D). Quiesced migration from the ADR-0011 layout preserves seqs/payloads and seals each migrated stream — the seal is the tail-erasure witness. Rejected: the ADR-0011 single-lineage event stream (all repos serialize through one head CAS, O(history) replay, lineage-wide damage); unfenced trim (unblocked only by 0001's versioned values); mode-A/mode-B fencing designs (reserved, not shipped); per-event tombstones; and for the crate itself, delivery/push/bus, forge types, and name registries — pull-only, opaque ids, the application maps names at its boundary. Flips if: retention needs grow past certified trim (a future fenced-retirement decision) or 0001's era model is superseded.\n" ;
		bedrock:timestamp "2026-08-21T10:51:16" .
	bedrock:vertex\/decision-0003-streaming-value-io a bedrock:ontology\/Decision ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/record\/decision-0003-streaming-value-io.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "ADR 0003: streaming-value I/O for AtomicKeyspace (superseded)" ;
		bedrock:references bedrock:vertex\/invariant-kernel-extension ;
		bedrock:source bedrock:path\/docs\/decisions\/0003-streaming-value-io.md ;
		bedrock:statement "The proposed v1 design for streaming large values through AtomicKeyspace: two representations behind one logical value API — inline v2 envelope up to 16 MiB; larger values as a v3 manifest in the key object plus immutable fixed-size SHA-256-addressed chunks in a kernel-private root; the manifest's conditional PUT the only commit point; readers always fetch and validate the control object first. Status at birth: PROPOSED / DRAFT — documentation only, no implementation authorized. Adjudication did not amend in place: the independent adversarial review (SHIP WITH AMENDMENTS) moved to a successor record. Superseded by ADR 0004 (decision-0004-streaming-value-io-v2), which kept the manifest/chunk architecture and amended it — this vertex is chain history, not live law; read the successor for what stands.\n" ;
		bedrock:timestamp "2026-08-22T20:43:22" .
	bedrock:vertex\/decision-0004-streaming-value-io-v2 a bedrock:ontology\/Decision ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/record\/decision-0004-streaming-value-io-v2.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "ADR 0004: streaming-value I/O v2 — manifest commit, bounded chunks" ;
		bedrock:references bedrock:vertex\/invariant-13-state , bedrock:vertex\/invariant-kernel-extension ;
		bedrock:requires bedrock:vertex\/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace ;
		bedrock:source bedrock:path\/docs\/decisions\/0004-streaming-value-io-v2.md ;
		bedrock:statement "Accepted 2026-08-22 via human-delegated synthesis (\"adopt the best solution derivable from both reviewers; reserve only physics-class forks for me\"). Supersedes ADR 0003, keeping its manifest/chunk architecture under ten review amendments (SHIP WITH AMENDMENTS -> SHIP, 10/10 fidelity, evidence verified). Synthesis-adopted rulings: (1) representation = manifest/chunks — the live Exoscale probe (run 32592980637, PARTIAL MULTIPART WITNESS) proved conditional completion works but part-addressed reads are measured absent, so the portable-correctness floor stands and any backend fast path is a future, capability-probed, feature-flagged addition; (2) CHUNK_BYTES = 16 MiB, INLINE_MAX = 64 MiB, chunk_count >= 2, 2x key-encoding bound, 892 B max key, and a 16 MiB encoded streams-envelope bound so streams-stay-inline is structural; (3) chunk GC is quiesced-only v1 with a cheap fence at a kernel-reserved key, the broken-quiescence data-loss race documented and demonstrated in the rig, and delete-free online orphan metering — quiescence is an operational assertion the kernel cannot prove; (4) per-key chunk scoping, global refcounted dedup rejected; (5) 64 MiB adapter guard on git whole-read paths, with object_exists()/FindHeader::try_header() as mandatory downstream migration sites; (6) key-late writes use a bounded ephemeral spool under the same guard, durable prepared-upload rejected. Hard edges: reserved-root guard rejects lineages naming keyspace or keyspace-chunks; stale-era eviction is conditional, never read-check-unconditional; the third lost-response outcome is Unavailable/ambiguous, never a fabricated conflict. Proof plan: A24-A35 on loopback + real-S3 legs. Rejected: native multipart at the logical key (no portable part reads), mutable LIST-discovered chunks (no atomic multi-object replacement; reopens ABA per chunk), temp-object + conditional copy (double bandwidth), global content-addressed dedup (crash-safe refcounting). Flip condition: a full witness of portable part-addressed/integrity reads would remove the manifest design's largest permanent liability (chunk GC) and reopen manifest-vs-native-multipart for a human ruling.\n" ;
		bedrock:supersedes bedrock:vertex\/decision-0003-streaming-value-io ;
		bedrock:timestamp "2026-08-22T20:43:22" .
	bedrock:vertex\/decision-0005-batched-deletion a bedrock:ontology\/Decision ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/record\/decision-0005-batched-deletion.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "ADR 0005: unconditional S3 multi-object deletion — typed outcomes, bounded chunks" ;
		bedrock:references bedrock:vertex\/decision-0004-streaming-value-io-v2 , bedrock:vertex\/invariant-kernel-extension , bedrock:vertex\/plan-batched-deletion-primitive , bedrock:vertex\/structure-kernel ;
		bedrock:requires bedrock:vertex\/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace ;
		bedrock:source bedrock:path\/docs\/decisions\/0005-batched-deletion.md ;
		bedrock:statement "Accepted 2026-08-23 by human merge of PR #33 (merge commit 60cb5c35) after a two-round independent adversarial review — both rounds returned AMEND (round two: G1-G5 plus five nitpicks) and landed as forward commits on the proposal branch; the final re-check at witness tip b3c13365 raised zero blocking findings. Chosen: additive AtomicKeyspace::delete_objects over S3 DeleteObjects beside the published delete_many — neither wraps the other; delete_many stays frozen (A6/G117) and not deprecated, and two response-trust implementations deliberately coexist (the legacy object_store path keeps its missing-member-defaults-to- success and unrequested-key panic residuals). Transport: sequential chunks of at most 1,000 keys under DELETE_OBJECTS_MAX_INPUT = 100_000, verbose responses only, exact per-chunk response bijection — no omitted key ever defaults to success; batch is transport, never transaction, and cross-key atomicity is a permanent non-goal. No batched conditional delete: delete_if_match remains the only conditional surface, per-key, permanently. Outcomes: one typed result per input key — Ok, Rejected, Unconfirmed, NotAttempted, Unsupported — behind an admission-only outer error; an Unconfirmed stop labels its untouched tail NotAttempted, a definitive mid-call refusal labels current chunk and tail Unsupported, and remaining() is checkpoint serialization, never retry policy. The primitive sits below lifecycle machinery: no tombstone, no incarnation bump, no fence read; its fence-blindness couples to ADR 0004 quiescence as the named residual — raw batch delete plus same-incarnation/version-0 recreate can re-materialize the exact chunk paths a concurrent sweep classified as orphaned, producing ADR 0004's forbidden ManifestIncomplete (witnessed as KeyspaceError::ChunkMissing; up to 1,000 controls per request). Claims A36-A45; a real-S3 DeleteObjects leg gates publication; implementation is one separately authorized kernel-extension batch targeting the next free 0.4.x. Rejected: mutating delete_many in place, wrapping delete_many over the new method, object_store::delete_stream for the assured path, one top-level wholesale error, read-then-delete, rollback/compensation (permanent). Flips if: a portable standards-level multi-object conditional (a per-object If-Match equivalent) emerges — that demands a superseding ADR with backend qualification, never a silent extension; cross-key transactionality stays out regardless.\n" ;
		bedrock:timestamp "2026-08-23T22:27:03" .
	bedrock:vertex\/epoch-20260823-9eb367706d13 a bedrock:ontology\/EpochRecord ;
		bedrock:commit "9eb367706d133866ec5005d0b4127ce1b282bf14" ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/record\/epoch-20260823-9eb367706d13.yamlld ;
		bedrock:mode "adopt" ;
		bedrock:offline false ;
		bedrock:statement "Everything after this commit operates under bedrock; prior history is reference, never law." ;
		bedrock:version "0.2.1" .
}

graph:definition {
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-01-possibility-space a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-01-possibility-space.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "Code is a possibility space" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "Code is a possibility space. A surface does everything it *can* do, not what its author meant. Work is collapsing possibilities to defined behavior. A green test proves a behavior exists — never that nothing else happens. Say what else could happen; declare what you did not collapse.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-02-gap-suspects a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-02-gap-suspects.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "A gap has three suspects" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "A gap has three suspects — the code, the requirement, or the instrument. Interrogate in the open before displacing any of them.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-03-situate-before-acting a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-03-situate-before-acting.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "Situate before acting; re-situate after" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "Situate before acting; re-situate after. Relationships carry unequal mass; the loudest, freshest signal is usually the smallest. Interrogate a contradiction before displacing what it contradicts. Authority attaches to landed sentences, not to your readings of them.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-04-completion-boundary a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-04-completion-boundary.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "Completion is behavior at the promised boundary" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "Completion is behavior at the promised boundary. Nothing in a deliverable is a stub, placeholder, or deferred branch. Not done: \"compiles\", \"structure in place\", \"foundation for later.\"\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-05-make-it-first a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-05-make-it-first.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "Make it first, prove it after" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:references bedrock:vertex\/breadcrumb-adversarial-review ;
		bedrock:statement "Make it first, prove it after. Build the slice, prove it, fix, continue. Teardown on demand, never a precondition. Deep adversarial review is human-invoked.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-06-regenerate-from-source a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-06-regenerate-from-source.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "Verify by regenerating from source" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "Verify by regenerating from source, never by reading the claim. Gate claims cite a CI run URL, never a local attestation.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-07-predeclare-criteria a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-07-predeclare-criteria.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "Predeclare criteria" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "Predeclare criteria before the run that answers them; judge results only against them. A refuted hypothesis is a successful experiment. Mixed outcomes stay mixed — never round toward a verdict. Timebox exploration; when the decision point arrives, resolve with what you have.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-08-dependency-boundary a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-08-dependency-boundary.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "The dependency boundary is the assurance boundary" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "The dependency boundary is the assurance boundary. What crosses it version-pinned is assured-by-default at that pin; you verify your *consumption*, never the dependency's internals — the same law root already held for adopted protocols (S3, Matrix, Git), generalized to every crate boundary. Pins are assured versions; bumps are deliberate acts. A missing capability at a consumed boundary is BLOCKING — stop and escalate; working around a boundary is the disqualifying failure.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-09-public-first a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-09-public-first.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "Public-first" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "Public-first. Before building inside, ask why this cannot be a public crate or repo; work backwards from that. Extract when the rubric passes; private only for named domain knowledge or secrets.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-10-git-rules a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-10-git-rules.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "Git: force push does not exist" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "Git: force push does not exist; nothing pushed is deleted; one writer per ref; PRs always — a human merges the default branch. Same policy in every repo.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-11-ci-rules a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-11-ci-rules.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "CI: one runner posture, the real suite" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "CI: every Linux/platform-neutral job runs on `org-ci-linux-x64`; WarpBuild only for native macOS/Windows artifacts (`warp-macos-15-arm64-6x`, `warp-windows-latest-x64-4x`); fork-PR code is mechanically rejected before runner assignment; a missing host tool is a P0 infrastructure defect — never install a hidden substitute; CI runs the real suite (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, locked build, nextest).\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-12-toolchain a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-12-toolchain.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "One fixed toolchain per repo" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "One fixed toolchain per repo, canonical task names; never invent a second one.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-13-state a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-13-state.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "State: one storage truth through the kernel" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "State: one storage truth through the kernel; records are immutable, created by conditional write; pointers move by CAS; every projection is rebuildable from records; reads are fenced; an integrity failure is never translated to absence.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-14-tailscale-first a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-14-tailscale-first.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "Tailscale-first" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "Tailscale-first: all internal reach rides the tailnet; SSH-over-Tailscale for operators; nothing internal is served outside it; public-IP access is break-glass only.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-15-decisions-append-only a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-15-decisions-append-only.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "Decisions are append-only" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "Decisions are append-only: ADRs are immutable — supersede, never edit.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-16-agents-md-register a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-16-agents-md-register.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "AGENTS.md is the register" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "AGENTS.md is the register: one screen of numbered invariants + \"where things live\" (graph epoch: generated from `situation/`, never hand-edited). After work that changes reality, re-situate it — emit knowledge, never rules.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-kernel-extension a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-kernel-extension.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "Kernel extension is human-gated" ;
		bedrock:layer "situated" ;
		bedrock:references bedrock:vertex\/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace ;
		bedrock:statement "A kernel change ships as ONE tightly scoped batch — the change, its contract suite, its proof — nothing else. Dispatches that touch the kernel state their human authorization explicitly and where the decision lives. Downstream breakage breaks definitively; repairs are separately orchestrated afterward. Do not bump the assured dependency pins casually (root Cargo.toml) — the kernel is assured at those versions.\n" .
	bedrock:vertex\/invariant-temp-work a bedrock:ontology\/Invariant ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/invariant-temp-work.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "Temp work lives under /Volumes/code/temp" ;
		bedrock:layer "situated" ;
		bedrock:statement "All scratch and temporary work lives under /Volumes/code/temp/ — nowhere else. Never mktemp, /tmp, /private/tmp, $TMPDIR, or any path on the boot drive (it is small and not ours to consume); git worktrees only in the sanctioned worktree locations; tools that default to a temp location get TMPDIR overridden or explicit output paths. When the task completes, remove what you created — leftover scratch is an incomplete delivery.\n" .
}
graph:plan {
	bedrock:vertex\/plan-batched-deletion-primitive a bedrock:ontology\/Plan ;
		bedrock:acceptance-criteria "A human accepts and merges ADR 0005; before acceptance, no Decision vertex or accepted-log entry represents it as closed law." , "A36-A45 pass in CI and a real-S3 witness proves checksum-compatible exact response bijection; refutation blocks publication." , "Deletion writes no tombstone or counter; fence-blind batch delete plus same-incarnation/version-0 recreate can reuse swept chunk paths, the named ADR 0004 residual." , "Invalid, incomplete, contradictory, or non-bijective responses never default an omitted key to success and never trigger per-key fallback." , "Published delete_many/delete/delete_if_match behavior remains unchanged; no batch is transactional or conditionally guarded." , "The API admits at most 100,000 unique keys, sends 1,000-key sequential chunks, retains only chunk-local paths, caps each diagnostic at 512 bytes, and shares request-level instances." , "The existing loopback bulk branch gains key-vector logging, key-less occurrence arms, configurable entry errors, whole-request cuts, and 405/501 refusal mode." , "The outcome vector preserves classification for bounded policy; remaining only serializes unresolved keys for durable checkpoints." , "The primitive uses caller-supplied keys only; LIST authority, durable job checkpoints, and epoch adoption remain outside it." , "Unconfirmed stops label only their untouched tail NotAttempted; a mid-call definitive refusal labels its current chunk and untouched tail Unsupported." ;
		bedrock:consumes bedrock:path\/crates\/yeetz-s3-kernel , bedrock:path\/crates\/yeetz-sdk-s3 , bedrock:path\/docs\/decisions\/0005-batched-deletion.md , bedrock:vertex\/decision-0001-atomic-keyspace , bedrock:vertex\/decision-0002-streams , bedrock:vertex\/decision-0004-streaming-value-io-v2 , bedrock:vertex\/invariant-08-dependency-boundary , bedrock:vertex\/invariant-13-state , bedrock:vertex\/invariant-kernel-extension , bedrock:vertex\/structure-kernel ;
		bedrock:disposition "{\"residual\":\"This draft does not assure acceptance, implementation authorization, A36-A45 behavior, provider qualification, publication, inventory/job completeness, or adoption. It leaves ADR 0004 quiescence external, including same-era chunk-path reuse, and keeps the weaker legacy response path live; outcome classification and bounded retry policy stay caller-owned.\\n\",\"state\":\"draft\"}"^^rdf:JSON ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/plan\/batched-deletion-primitive.yamlld ;
		bedrock:intent "Carry ADR 0005 through adversarial review and human acceptance, then — only under a separately authorized kernel-extension batch — deliver an additive AtomicKeyspace primitive for 1,000-key S3 DeleteObjects transport with honest per-key partial outcomes and unchanged single-key atomicity law.\n" ;
		bedrock:label "Plan: propose typed S3 multi-object deletion" ;
		bedrock:oracle bedrock:path\/docs\/decisions\/0005-batched-deletion.md ;
		bedrock:reflect-depth 2 ;
		bedrock:source bedrock:path\/docs\/decisions\/0005-batched-deletion.md ;
		bedrock:tasks "Extend the existing loopback bulk branch with key-vector logging, key-less occurrence arms, configurable entry errors, request cuts, and refusal mode; prove A36-A45 and real-S3 qualification." , "Implement the bounded direct-SDK seam and additive AtomicKeyspace API without migrating or strengthening existing methods." , "Keep ADR 0005 explicitly proposed and register it only as this draft plan." , "Obtain human acceptance and merge; only then register ADR 0005 as a Decision and add it to the accepted structure log." , "Obtain separate human authorization for one firewalled kernel implementation batch." , "Publish the next free 0.4.x closure release; orchestrate every downstream adoption separately." , "Run the independent adversarial review and amend the proposal forward where required." ;
		bedrock:witnesses "https://github.com/cleverunicornz/yeetz-s3-kernel/actions/runs/32665465723" .
}

Append-only; supersede, never edit. Each is registered as a Decision vertex in situation/record/ (decision-0001… decision-0005); liveness is read from the supersedes chain — 0001, 0002, 0004, and 0005 are live, 0003 is superseded by 0004. graph:definition {
	bedrock:vertex\/term-promise-witness-oracle a bedrock:ontology\/Term ;
		bedrock:document bedrock:path\/situation\/definition\/term-promise-witness-oracle.yamlld ;
		bedrock:label "promise, oracle, witness, residual" ;
		bedrock:layer "floor" ;
		bedrock:statement "A promise states behavior; an oracle judges promise against actual. A witness is the retained observation of one run and proves existence, never exclusivity. Residual is what was deliberately not assured, declared so everyone sees the line of demarcation — we assure the positive space only; the negative space is infinite.\n" .
}
